newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TENNIS-SOUTH AFRICA CLINCH PLACE IN SECOND ROUND.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SOUTH AFRICA CLINCH PLACE IN SECOND ROUND.

text.p: South Africa lined up a probable second round tie away to Sweden in April after a four-set victory over Russia in their Davis Cup World Group first round doubles match on Sunday.

The South African pair of Ellis Ferreira and Grant Stafford outclassed the Russian combination of Andrei Olhovsky and Andrei Cherkasov 6-2 3-6 6-0 6-2 to give the home side an unassailable 3-0 lead in the tie.

"It's a great feeling to have won this tie. We were expected to win but, so far, all the matches here have been tough. This victory is very satisfying," Danie Visser, South Africa's non-playing team captain said.

On-court temperatures reached 42 degrees celsius as the South Africans swept through the first set 6-2 in only half an hour, with the left-handed Ferreira winning several points on crunching forehand drives.
The Russians fought back with three breaks of serve to take the second set 6-3 as Olhovsky, ranked 23rd in world doubles, began to mix powerful ground strokes with some intelligently-placed lobs.
"They threw up a lot of lobs in that set and, for quite a while, the sun was right in our faces in the middle of the court," Ferreira said. "But, once the sun moved, it wasn't that bad."

The South Africans then upped a few gears to breeze through the next two sets 6-0, 6-2 in only 45 minutes. They broke the Russians three times in the third set and twice in the fourth to seal overall victory for their country in the tie.
